question.problem:
A rectangular plate occupies the region
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 2,\,\,1\le y\le 2\}$
with mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=x+1.$ Find the moment of inertia of this plate about the line $y=1.$
question.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $y=1$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|y-1|.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $y=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}(x+1)|y-1{|}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}(x+1)(y-1)^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{[\frac{(x+1)^{2}}{2}(y-1)^{2}]}_{-1}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{9}{2}(y-1)^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{3(y-1)^{3}}{2}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}-0 \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
